issue.title: rqt_controller_manager stuck
issue.body: **Describe the bug** The rqt_controller_manager plugin is unusable after a few seconds is running. The UI becomes unresponsive and it gets stuck. The function `_update_controllers` seem to take increasingly more time to execute. At some point it takes more time than the Timer and it gets very slow. Here you can see the execution time increasing: **To Reproduce** Steps to reproduce the behavior: 1. `ros2 run rqt_controller_manager rqt_controller_manager` 2. Wait ca. 10-20 seconds 3. Try any operation on the gui **Environment (please complete the following information):** - OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker container) - Version Jazzy Thank you for your great work!
issue.bodyHTML:
Describe the bug
The rqt_controller_manager plugin is unusable after a few seconds is running. The UI becomes unresponsive and it gets stuck. The function _update_controllers seem to take increasingly more time to execute. At some point it takes more time than the Timer and it gets very slow. Here you can see the execution time increasing:

To Reproduce
Steps to reproduce the behavior:

  1. ros2 run rqt_controller_manager rqt_controller_manager
  2. Wait ca. 10-20 seconds
  3. Try any operation on the gui

Environment (please complete the following information):

  • OS: Ubuntu 24.04 (Docker container)
  • Version Jazzy

Thank you for your great work!

comments.body:
From my experience the issue persists. The ros2_control_node has been running constantly.
I have removed/commented the following lines:

 https://github.com/ros-controls/ros2_control/blob/b3075dc13a2d505ebfb1d43459afab9ca59ec9a6/rqt_controller_manager/rqt_controller_manager/controller_manager.py#L204-L210

This way it takes a longer time until the rqt_cm gets stuck but it still does after a few minutes, bringing down the entire OS.

On another note, I have a panel plugin for RViz, in which I subscribe to _/~/activity_ and use the _~/set_hardware_component_state_, _/~/switch_controller_, _/~/configure_controller_ services, also here after a while (a few minutes) the Rviz frame rate drops to close to zero and Rviz consumes all CPU. If I close the panel, RViz recovers. (I am not 100% certain as this can obviously also another bug in my code but the symptoms are very similar)

Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL2 on Windows
rqt_controller_manager: Jazzy 4.38.0
comments.bodyHTML:
From my experience the issue persists. The ros2_control_node has been running constantly.
I have removed/commented the following lines:

ros2_control/rqt_controller_manager/rqt_controller_manager/controller_manager.py

Lines 204 to 210 in b3075dc

# Append potential controller configs found in the node's parameters
for name in _get_parameter_controller_names(self._node, self._cm_name):
add_ctrl = all(name != ctrl.name for ctrl in controllers)
if add_ctrl:
type_str = _get_controller_type(self._node, self._cm_name, name)
uninit_ctrl = ControllerState(name=name, type=type_str)
controllers.append(uninit_ctrl)

This way it takes a longer time until the rqt_cm gets stuck but it still does after a few minutes, bringing down the entire OS.

On another note, I have a panel plugin for RViz, in which I subscribe to /~/activity and use the ~/set_hardware_component_state, /~/switch_controller, /~/configure_controller services, also here after a while (a few minutes) the Rviz frame rate drops to close to zero and Rviz consumes all CPU. If I close the panel, RViz recovers. (I am not 100% certain as this can obviously also another bug in my code but the symptoms are very similar)

Ubuntu 24.04 in WSL2 on Windows
rqt_controller_manager: Jazzy 4.38.0
